nodes.title: THE HOMERIC HYMN TO DEMETER  /  AN INCOMPLETE RETURN

Persephone:
a return with a cost
The hymn marks her unwillingness. This is an abduction, not a voluntary romantic departure.
Demeter searches
nodes.text: Her daughter is missing. Hecate and Helios help reveal what happened.

nodes.title: Hades takes her
nodes.text: The earth opens. Persephone cries for help. Zeus has authorized the seizure.

nodes.title: Persephone
nodes.text: Persephone rises toward Demeter with Hermes and Hekate. Attic, ca. 440 BCE. Met 28.57.23. An image interprets the story.

nodes.title: Demeter's famine
nodes.text: Demeter withholds grain. Human survival and divine honors are endangered.

nodes.title: Zeus sends Hermes
nodes.text: Return becomes possible, but the pomegranate prevents a permanent stay above.

nodes.title: One third below. Two thirds above.
nodes.text: The hymn reunites mother and daughter for part of each year. Its settlement gives no familiar modern six-seed arrangement.
